question: What are the two primary organs that make up the central nervous system?
explanation: The central nervous system is strictly composed of the brain and the spinal cord, separating it from the peripheral nervous system. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the main function of neuroglia cells in the nervous system?

options.A: To release hormones straight into the bloodstream
options.B: To support, protect, and nourish neurons
options.C: To generate electrical impulses for muscle movement
options.D: To carry signals directly from the skin to the brain

explanation: Neuroglia do not send nerve signals themselves; instead, they act as support staff that protect and feed the active neurons. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the name of the tough, leather-like outermost layer of the meninges?
explanation: The dura mater forms the heavy outer protective shield right beneath the skull bones. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why does a patient not feel pain when a surgeon touches the actual brain tissue during a procedure?

options.B: The brain tissue lacks pain receptors
options.C: The skull blocks pain signals from escaping
options.D: The dura mater numbs the rest of the brain

explanation: Because brain tissue has no nociceptors, pain is only felt when surrounding structures like the scalp, blood vessels, or meninges are irritated. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which lobe of the cerebral cortex is primarily responsible for processing visual information?
explanation: The back of the brain, known as the occipital lobe, specializes in receiving and making sense of what the eyes see. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h3)

question: A patient suffers a stroke affecting their left frontal lobe. What problem are they most likely to experience?

options.A: Loss of feeling in the lower legs

explanation: The frontal lobe houses motor control areas, including the region responsible for producing speech. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which brain structure acts as the main relay station for sorting incoming sensory information?
explanation: The thalamus filters and relays sensory signals up to the correct regions of the cerebral cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is serious injury to the medulla oblongata considered immediately life-threatening?

options.A: It controls vital autonomic functions like breathing and heart rate
options.B: It produces all visual images for the eyes
options.C: It stores all long-term memories for daily living
options.D: It coordinates voluntary balance during walking

explanation: The medulla houses the respiratory and cardiac centers that keep a person breathing and maintain blood pressure automatically. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary role of the cerebellum in the nervous system?

options.A: Coordinating smooth muscle movement and balance
options.B: Processing conscious thoughts and logical reasoning
options.C: Regulating basic body temperature and hunger
options.D: Relaying pain signals from the skin to the brain

explanation: The cerebellum ensures that physical movements are smooth, balanced, and properly timed. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h5)

question: A patient stumbles when walking and cannot coordinate their finger-to-nose movement during a physical exam. Which brain structure is most likely impaired?
explanation: Inability to perform smooth coordinated movements or maintain balance points directly to cerebellar dysfunction. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h5)

question: Where is the gray matter located in the cross-section of the spinal cord?

options.C: On the outer surface as tracts
options.D: On the inside in an H-shape

explanation: Unlike the brain where gray matter is on the outside, the spinal cord places its gray matter on the inside surrounded by white matter. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of a spinal reflex loop like pulling your hand away from a hot stove?

options.A: It increases blood flow directly to the burned finger
options.B: It stores the memory of the hot stove permanently
options.C: It bypasses the brain to prevent delayed injury
options.D: It activates the hypothalamus to raise body temperature

explanation: Reflexes skip the time-consuming process of brain thinking, allowing lightning-fast muscle reactions to protect the body from harm. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary function of cerebrospinal fluid?

options.A: To transmit electrical signals across synapses
options.B: To cushion the brain and provide nutritional support
options.C: To produce red blood cells for nervous tissue
options.D: To cool down the body during a high fever

explanation: CSF acts as a shock-absorbing liquid cushion while also nourishing the central nervous system tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why does the blood-brain barrier present a major hurdle when treating certain brain infections?

options.A: It actively destroys all types of antibiotics in the blood
options.B: It prevents many helpful medicines from entering brain tissue
options.C: It increases the pressure of cerebrospinal fluid dangerously
options.D: It allows bacteria to hide safely inside the ventricles

explanation: The same tight barriers that keep harmful toxins out also block many beneficial pharmaceutical drugs from reaching infections inside the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h7)
